'''Narinder Singh Kapany''' (31 October 1926 – 4 December 2020) was an [[Indian-American]] [[physicist]] and a pioneer in the field of [[fiber optics]]. Notably, Kapany is known for coining and popularising the term "fiber optics".<ref name="ucsc.edu">{{cite web|title=Narinder Singh Kapany Chair in Opto-electronics|url=http://southasia.ucsc.edu/endowed-chairs/narinder-singh-kapany.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170521222508/http://southasia.ucsc.edu/endowed-chairs/narinder-singh-kapany.html|archive-date=21 May 2017|access-date=20 May 2017|publisher=University of California Santa Cruz}}.</ref><ref name="forbes.com">{{cite magazine|last=Dharmakumar|first=Rohin|date=11 March 2011|title=Lighting up the Last Mile|url=https://www.forbes.com/2011/03/16/forbes-india-high-speed-connectivity-with-optical-fibers.html|url-status=live|magazine=Forbes India|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190728120034/https://www.forbes.com/2011/03/16/forbes-india-high-speed-connectivity-with-optical-fibers.html|archive-date=28 July 2019|access-date=5 September 2017}}</ref> ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'' named him one of seven "Unsung Heroes of the 20th Century" for his [[Nobel Prize]]-deserving invention.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Unsung Heroes They may not be household names, but without the contributions of these individuals, the business landscape would look radically different today. – November 22, 1999|url=https://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/1999/11/22/269122/index.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619042255/http://money.cnn.com/magazines/fortune/fortune_archive/1999/11/22/269122/index.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 June 2009|access-date=2021-01-27|website=archive.fortune.com}}</ref><ref name="rediff.com: Honouring the Achievers">[http://specials.rediff.com/news/2004/jan/09sld03.htm rediff.com: Honouring the Achievers] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180603115121/http://specials.rediff.com/news/2004/jan/09sld03.htm|date=3 June 2018}}. ==Early life and research==
[[File:Photograph of the Kapany family, circa late 19th century.jpg|thumb|Photograph of the Kapany family, circa late 19th century. Pictured is the grandfather (centre), great-grandfather (left), and great-grandmother (right) of Narinder Singh Kapany of Moga, Punjab.]]
Kapany was born on 31 October 1926, in [[Moga, Punjab|Moga]], Punjab to Sundar Singh and Kundan Kaur. He was from a [[Sikh]] [[Khatri]] family of [[Sodhi]] clan and were [[Zamindar|landlords]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Kapany |first=Narinder |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TZFOEAAAQBAJ |title=Narinder Singh Kapany: The Man Who Bent Light |year=2021 |publisher=Roli Books Private Limited |isbn=978-93-92130-00-7 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="indiatoday.intoday.in" /> The family claims to be descended from [[Guru Amar Das]], the third [[Sikh gurus|guru]] of the Sikhs, through the guru's son Mohari.{{Efn|Mohari's name is alternatively spelt as 'Mohri'.|group=note}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Mann |first=Gurinder Singh |url=http://www.sikhfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/Sikh_Art_from_the_Kapany_Collection_full.pdf |title=Sikh Art from the Kapany Collection |publisher=The Sikh Foundation |year=2017 |isbn=9780970036346 |edition=1st |pages=30 |chapter=2. Narinder Singh Kapany: The Man and His Accomplishments}}</ref> In c.1760, the family shifted to Nizamabad in Uttar Pradesh.<ref name=":0" /> He completed his schooling in [[Dehradun]] and went on to graduate from [[Agra University]].<ref name="indiatoday.intoday.in">{{cite web|last=Sharma|first=Dinesh C.|date=15 October 2009|title=Nobel Question Mark|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/latest-headlines/story/nobel-question-mark-58572-2009-10-14|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117022729/http://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/Nobel+question+mark/1/66364.html|archive-date=17 November 2015|access-date=20 May 2017|publisher=India Today|location=New Delhi}}</ref><ref name="NYTProfile">{{cite web |last1=Risen |first1=Clay |title=Narinder S. Kapany, 'Father of Fiber Optics,' Dies at 94 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/07/technology/narinder-s-kapany-dead.html |website=The New York Times |date=7 January 2021 |access-date=10 January 2021 |archive-date=10 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210210145758/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/07/technology/narinder-s-kapany-dead.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He served as an [[Indian Ordnance Factories Service]] officer, before going to [[Imperial College London]] in 1952 to work on a Ph.D. degree in optics from the [[University of London]], which he obtained in 1955.<ref name="indiatoday.intoday.in"/><ref name=":1" />

At [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]], Kapany worked with [[Harold Hopkins (physicist)|Harold Hopkins]] on transmission through fibers, achieving good image transmission through a large bundle of optical fibers for the first time in 1953.<ref name=Hecht2004>{{cite book |first=Jeff |last=Hecht |title=City of Light: The Story of Fiber Optics |url=https://archive.org/details/citylightstoryfi00hech_258 |url-access=limited |publisher=Oxford University |edition=revised |date=2004 |isbn=9780195162554 |pages=[https://archive.org/details/citylightstoryfi00hech_258/page/n67 55]–70}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Hopkins, H. H. |author2=Kapany, N. S. |name-list-style=amp |journal=Nature|doi=10.1038/173039b0 |volume=173|pages= 39–41 |year=1954 |title=A flexible fibrescope, using static scanning|issue=4392|bibcode = 1954Natur.173...39H |s2cid=4275331 }}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110629061117/http://nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/2009/sciback_phy_09.pdf Two Revolutionary Optical Technologies]. Scientific Background on the Nobel Prize in Physics 2009. Nobelprize.org. 6 October 2009</ref> Optical fibers had been tried for image transmission before, but Hopkins and Kapany's technique allowed much better image quality than could previously be achieved. This, combined with the almost-simultaneous development of [[Cladding (fiber optics)|optical cladding]] by Dutch scientist Bram van Heel, helped jump start the new field of [[fibre optics|fiber optics]]. Kapany coined the term 'fiber optics' in an article in ''[[Scientific American]]'' in 1960, wrote the first book about the new field, and was the new field's most prominent researcher, writer, and spokesperson.<ref name=Hecht2004/><ref>[http://news.rediff.com/report/2009/oct/08/how-india-missed-another-nobel-prize.htm How India missed another Nobel Prize – Rediff.com India News] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214122132/https://news.rediff.com/report/2009/oct/08/how-india-missed-another-nobel-prize.htm |date=14 December 2019 }}. News.rediff.com (12 October 2009). Retrieved on 8 February 2017.</ref><ref name="auto2">{{Cite web|date=3 May 2017|title=Asian American Pacific Islander Heritage Month: The Father of Fiber Optics|url=https://transportationhistory.org/2017/05/03/asian-american-pacific-islander-heritage-month-the-father-of-fiber-optics/|access-date=12 June 2020|website=Transportation History|language=en|archive-date=12 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612161936/https://transportationhistory.org/2017/05/03/asian-american-pacific-islander-heritage-month-the-father-of-fiber-optics/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kapany's research and work encompassed fiber-optics communications, lasers, biomedical instrumentation, solar energy and pollution monitoring. He had over 120 patents, and was a member of the [[National Inventors Council]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|last=Stephens|first=Tim|title=Narinder Kapany, known as the 'father of fiber optics,' dies at 94|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2020/12/narinder-kapany-in-memoriam.html|access-date=2021-01-27|website=UC Santa Cruz News|language=en|archive-date=1 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201013734/https://news.ucsc.edu/2020/12/narinder-kapany-in-memoriam.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He was an International [[Fellow]]<ref name="List of Fellows"/> of numerous scientific societies including the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]],<ref name="List of Fellows"/> the [[Optical Society of America]], and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Narinder Singh Kapany Chair in Opto-electronics|url=https://southasia.ucsc.edu/endowed-chairs/narinder-singh-kapany.html|access-date=5 December 2020|website=southasia.ucsc.edu|archive-date=16 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116162425/https://southasia.ucsc.edu/endowed-chairs/narinder-singh-kapany.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Fibreoptic.jpg|thumb|Optical fibers]]
As an entrepreneur and business executive, Kapany specialized in the processes of innovation and the management of technology and technology transfer. In 1960, he founded Optics Technology Inc. and was chairman of the board, president, and director of research for twelve years. In 1967 the company went public with numerous corporate acquisitions and joint-ventures in the United States and abroad. In 1973, Kapany founded Kaptron Inc. and was president and CEO until 1990 when he sold the company to [[AMP Incorporated]]. For the next nine years, Kapany was an AMP Fellow, heading the Entrepreneur & Technical Expert Program and serving as chief technologist for global communications business. He founded K2 Optronics. He also served on the boards of various companies. He was a member of the Young Presidents Organization and later a member of the World Presidents Organization.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Service|first=Tribune News|title=Father of fibre optics and patron of Sikh arts Narinder Singh Kapany dies at 94|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/diaspora/father-of-fibre-optics-and-patron-of-sikh-arts-narinder-singh-kapany-dies-at-94-179849|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201204221550/https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/diaspora/father-of-fibre-optics-and-patron-of-sikh-arts-narinder-singh-kapany-dies-at-94-179849|archive-date=4 December 2020|access-date=5 December 2020|website=Tribuneindia News Service|language=en}}</ref>

As an academic, Kapany taught and supervised research activity of postgraduate students. He was a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]]. He founded the Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurial Development (CIED) at UCSC<ref name="auto"/> and served as director for seven years. At [[Stanford University]], he was a visiting scholar in the Physics Department and consulting professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering.<ref name="auto2"/>

As an author and lecturer, Kapany published over 100 scientific papers and four books on opto-electronics and [[entrepreneurship]].

==Philanthropy and art==
As a [[Philanthropy|philanthropist]], Kapany was active in education and the arts. He was the founding chairman of the Sikh Foundation and a major funder of its activities for over 50 years.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sikhfoundation.org/about-us/ |title=About Us |publisher=Sikh Foundation |access-date=20 May 2017 |archive-date=22 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170522162302/http://www.sikhfoundation.org/about-us/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In collaboration with international institutions and publishers, the Foundation runs programs in publishing, academia and the arts.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sikh Arts – The Sikh Foundation International|url=http://www.sikhfoundation.org/sikh-arts/|access-date=5 December 2020|language=en-CA|archive-date=1 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201201211842/http://www.sikhfoundation.org/sikh-arts/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1998, Kapany endowed a Chair of [[Sikh Studies]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]. His gift in 1999 of $500,000 to the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco established a gallery in its new building displaying the works he donated from his collection of [[Sikh art]].<ref name="auto3">{{Cite web|title=The Sikh Foundation – Community Profiles|url=http://www.sikhfoundation.org/comprof0602.html|access-date=5 December 2020|website=www.sikhfoundation.org|archive-date=28 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228211900/http://www.sikhfoundation.org/comprof0602.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Saints and Kings: Arts, Culture, and Legacy of the Sikhs {{!}} Exhibitions {{!}} Asian Art Museum|url=https://exhibitions.asianart.org/exhibitions/saints-and-kings-arts-culture-and-legacy-of-the-sikhs/|access-date=5 December 2020|website=Exhibitions|language=en-US|archive-date=14 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514015437/https://exhibitions.asianart.org/exhibitions/saints-and-kings-arts-culture-and-legacy-of-the-sikhs/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Reporter|first=SUNITA SOHRABJI/India-West Staff|title=Sikh Foundation Celebrates 50th Anniversary with Exhibit at Asian Art Museum|url=https://www.indiawest.com/news/global_indian/sikh-foundation-celebrates-50th-anniversary-with-exhibit-at-asian-art-museum/article_3942de84-f46c-11e6-bbae-9fb6e3687a60.html|access-date=5 December 2020|website=India West|language=en|archive-date=9 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209070837/https://www.indiawest.com/news/global_indian/sikh-foundation-celebrates-50th-anniversary-with-exhibit-at-asian-art-museum/article_3942de84-f46c-11e6-bbae-9fb6e3687a60.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1999, he endowed a Chair of Optoelectronics at the [[University of California, Santa Cruz]]. Again in 2012, he established the Narinder Kapany Endowed Chair in Entrepreneurship at UC Santa Cruz.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Stephens|first=Tim|title=Gift from Narinder Kapany establishes endowed chair in entrepreneurship|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2012/11/kapany-chair.html|access-date=2020-12-11|website=UC Santa Cruz News|language=en|archive-date=12 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612160816/https://news.ucsc.edu/2012/11/kapany-chair.html|url-status=live}}</ref>  He was a trustee of the University of California, Santa Cruz Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Rappaport|first=Scott|title=Gift from Narinder Kapany will establish Sikh book collection and study room at McHenry Library|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2017/03/kapany-library-sikh-gift.html|access-date=12 June 2020|website=UC Santa Cruz News|language=en|archive-date=12 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612160816/https://news.ucsc.edu/2017/03/kapany-library-sikh-gift.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He also served as a trustee of the [[Menlo School]] in [[Menlo Park, California|Menlo Park]], California.<ref name=":2" />

As an art collector, Kapany specialised in Sikh art. He provided paintings and other objects on loan for the "Arts of the Sikh Kingdoms" exhibition, which was held at London's Victoria & Albert Museum beginning in March 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Victoria and Albert Museum|first=Online Museum|date=11 January 2011|title=The Art of the Sikh Kingdoms|url=http://www.vam.ac.uk/content/journals/conservation-journal/issue-31/the-art-of-the-sikh-kingdoms/|access-date=12 June 2020|website=www.vam.ac.uk|archive-date=12 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612162407/http://www.vam.ac.uk/content/journals/conservation-journal/issue-31/the-art-of-the-sikh-kingdoms/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":43">{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Tarlochan |date=12 May 2026 |title=PROMOTORS OF SIKHI: Global Sikhs Preserving Sikh Heritage |url=https://sikhnet.com/news/promotors-sikhi |access-date=13 September 2026 |website=[[SikhNet]]}}</ref> From there, the exhibition proceeded to the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (with the Sikh Foundation as a sponsor) and opened in May 2000 at the [[Royal Ontario Museum]] in Toronto. The exhibition follows "Splendors of the Punjab: Sikh Art and Literature in 1992" organised by Kapany in collaboration with the Asian Art Museum and UC Berkeley to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the Sikh Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sikh Art and Literature|url=http://www.caareviews.org/reviews/91|access-date=12 June 2020|website=Sikh Art and Literature|archive-date=12 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612162407/http://www.caareviews.org/reviews/91|url-status=live}}</ref> As an artist, Kapany's 'dynoptic' sculptures were displayed at the Exploratorium of the [[Palace of Fine Arts]] in San Francisco in 1972 and at museums and art galleries in Chicago, Monterey, Palo Alto, and Stanford.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sikh Art Museum mooted for BC {{!}} South Asian Post {{!}} Indo Canadian newspaper – Vancouver, Surrey, Calgary, Toronto, Brampton, Edmonton, Winnipeg, Montreal|url=https://www.southasianpost.com/article/5518-sikh-art-museum-mooted-bc.html|access-date=5 December 2020|website=www.southasianpost.com|archive-date=5 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205012707/https://www.southasianpost.com/article/5518-sikh-art-museum-mooted-bc.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="auto3"/> In 1999, Kapany donated $500,000 to the Asian Art Museum in San Francisco to establish a Sikh gallery at the museum and donated a hundred Sikh artworks, artefacts, and objects from his collection for the purpose. On 27 October 2022, an enlarged Sikh gallery at the Asian Art Museum was inaugurated, with the enlarged gallery being named after Satinder Kaur, Kapany's wife.<ref name=":43" />

==Awards and recognition==
Kapany was posthumously included in the list of Padma Vibhushan awardees<ref>{{Cite web |title=Padma Awards 2021 announced |url=https://pib.gov.in/pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1692337 |access-date=2023-09-20 |website=pib.gov.in |language=en}}</ref> for 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Punjab born Indian-American Sikh scientist gets Padma Vibhushan posthumously |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/chandigarh/punjab-born-indian-american-sikh-scientist-padma-vibhushan-posthumously-7161942/#:~:text=Punjab%20born%20scientist%20Narinder%20Singh,He%20was%2094. |work=The Indian Express |date=26 January 2021 |language=en |access-date=12 February 2021 |archive-date=20 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210220191806/https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/chandigarh/punjab-born-indian-american-sikh-scientist-padma-vibhushan-posthumously-7161942/#:~:text=Punjab%20born%20scientist%20Narinder%20Singh,He%20was%2094. |url-status=live }}</ref> The award is India's second highest civilian honor. He received the UC Santa Cruz Foundation Fiat Lux Award in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fiat Lux Award|url=https://foundation.ucsc.edu/awards/fiat-lux-award.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612160818/https://foundation.ucsc.edu/awards/fiat-lux-award.html|archive-date=12 June 2020|access-date=12 June 2020|website=foundation.ucsc.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Stephens|first=Tim|title=Gift from Narinder Kapany establishes endowed chair in entrepreneurship|url=https://news.ucsc.edu/2012/11/kapany-chair.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612160816/https://news.ucsc.edu/2012/11/kapany-chair.html|archive-date=12 June 2020|access-date=12 June 2020|website=UC Santa Cruz News|language=en}}</ref> He was also the recipient of the [[Pravasi Bharatiya Samman]] in 2004. He received the Excellence 2000 Award from the USA Pan-Asian American Chamber of Commerce in 1998. In November 1999, he was identified by ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'' as one of the seven "unsung heroes who greatly influenced life in the twentieth century" in the "Businessmen of the Century" issue. Dr. Kapany was also on Time Magazine's list of top ten scientists of the 20th century in Time's last issue of 1999.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boitano|first1=Margaret|last2=Carvell|first2=Tim|date=22 November 1999|title=Unsung Heroes|journal=Fortune Magazine|pages=144–146<!-- |via=EBSCO --><!-- Needs supporting url --> }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jewels of Punjab – Dr Narinder Singh Kapany – The Sikh Foundation International|date=23 December 2017 |url=https://www.sikhfoundation.org/jewels-of-punjab-dr-narinder-singh-kapany/|access-date=5 December 2020|language=en-CA|archive-date=27 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027035654/http://www.sikhfoundation.org/jewels-of-punjab-dr-narinder-singh-kapany/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Kapany married Satinder Kaur in 1954, in London.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite web|last=Service|first=Tribune News|title=Scientist, Entrepreneur, Philanthropist|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/scientist-entrepreneur-philanthropist-180142|access-date=5 December 2020|website=Tribuneindia News Service|language=en|archive-date=5 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205024518/https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/scientist-entrepreneur-philanthropist-180142|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="NYTProfile" /> She died in 2016 after a long battle against Parkinson's disease.<ref name="satinder_kaur">{{Cite web|title=A Portrait of Elegance and Grace – Satinder Kaur Kapany|url=https://www.sikhfoundation.org/a-portrait-of-elegance-grace-satinder-kaur-kapany/|access-date=21 April 2024|website=www.sikhfoundation.org|date=29 June 2016 |language=en}}</ref> The couple had a daughter named Kiki Kapany, who now runs the Sikh Foundation.<ref name=":43" />

==Death==
Kapany died on 4 December 2020, aged 94 in [[Redwood City, California|Redwood City]], California.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Singh |first=Kamal P. |date=June 2021 |title=In memory of Narinder Singh Kapany |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41566-021-00812-z |journal=Nature Photonics |language=en |volume=15 |issue=6 |pages=403–404 |doi=10.1038/s41566-021-00812-z |bibcode=2021NaPho..15..403S |issn=1749-4893|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Haldar|first=Raktim|title=Dr Narinder Singh Kapany: Forgotten 'Father of Fiber-Optics'|url=http://nopr.niscair.res.in/handle/123456789/55907|access-date=2021-01-08|website=Science Reporter|language=en|archive-date=2 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210802234342/http://nopr.niscair.res.in/handle/123456789/55907|url-status=live}}</ref>
